_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 29 (Jacob at Laban's well; marries Leah/Rachel; first sons). Saadia-specific: v.31 'משנייה' = 'hated' (Saadia preserves the difficult ויאהבני אישי / שנואה reading); v.32 'צ'עף' = 'weakness/affliction' (= B16:11 — Saadia's gloss for עניי); v.33 'סמיע' = 'attentive listener' (substitutes for ויראני אלהים which would be inappropriate).

translations.1: And Jacob lifted up his feet, and went to the land of the people of the east.
translations.2: And he looked — and behold, a well in the wilderness; and there were three flocks of sheep crouching by it — for from it they watered the flocks. And a great stone was upon its mouth.
translations.3: And when all the herdsmen of the flocks were gathered there, they would roll the stone from the mouth of the well, and water the sheep; then they returned it to its place.
translations.4: Jacob said to them: 'Where are you from, my brothers?' They said: 'We are from Haran.'
translations.5: He said to them: 'Do you know Laban the son of Nahor?' They said: 'Yes.'
translations.6: He said: 'Is he in good health?' They said: 'Yes. And behold, Rachel his daughter is coming with the sheep.'
translations.7: And he said to them: 'Behold, the day is still long; it is not the time for the cattle to be gathered. Water the sheep, and go pasture them.'
translations.8: They said: 'We cannot do that, until the herdsmen of the flocks gather, and roll the stone from the mouth of the well; then we water the sheep.'
translations.9: While he was still speaking with them, Rachel arrived with her father's sheep — for she was a shepherdess.
translations.10: And when Jacob saw Rachel, the daughter of Laban his maternal uncle, and the sheep of Laban his maternal uncle, he drew near and rolled the stone from the mouth of the well, and watered his flock.
translations.11: And Jacob kissed Rachel, and lifted up his voice, and wept.
translations.12: And he told her that he was the son of her father's sister, the son of Rebekah; and she ran and told her father.
translations.13: And when Laban heard the news of Jacob, his sister's son, he ran to meet him, and embraced him, and kissed him, and brought him into his house; and he told Laban all these things.
translations.14: Laban said to him: 'Surely you are my bone and my flesh.' And he stayed with him a month of days.
translations.15: Then Laban said to him: 'Just because you are my kinsman, shall you serve me for nothing? Tell me what is your wage.'
translations.16: And Laban had two daughters; the name of the elder was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.
translations.17: And the eyes of Leah were beautiful; and Rachel was beautiful both of form and of appearance.
translations.18: And Jacob loved Rachel, and said: 'I shall serve you seven years for Rachel your younger daughter.'
translations.19: Laban said: 'It is more fitting that I give her to you than that I give her to another man; stay with me.'
translations.21: Then Jacob said to him: 'Give me my wife, for my days have been completed; let me enter to her.'
translations.22: And Laban gathered the people of his place, and made them a feast.
translations.23: And when it was evening, he took Leah his daughter, and brought her to him; and he came in to her.
translations.24: And he gave her Zilpah his maidservant, to be a maidservant for her.
translations.25: And in the morning — behold, it was Leah; and he said to Laban: 'What is this you have done to me? Did I not serve you for Rachel? Why have you deceived me?'
translations.26: He said: 'It is not done so in our land — to give the younger before the elder.
translations.27: Complete the week of this one, and we shall give you this one also, for a service that you shall serve me another seven years.'
translations.28: And Jacob did so, and completed her week; and he gave him Rachel his daughter, to be his wife.
translations.29: And Laban gave to Rachel his daughter Bilhah his maidservant, to be a maidservant for her.
translations.30: And he came also to Rachel; and he loved her more than Leah. And he served him yet another seven years.
translations.31: And God knew that Leah was hated; and He granted her a child. And Rachel was barren.
translations.32: And Leah conceived, and bore a son; and she named him Reuben — for she said: 'God has looked upon my affliction; now my husband will love me.'
translations.33: And she conceived again, and bore a son; she said: 'God is an attentive listener — for I am hated; and He has granted me this one also.' And she named him Simeon.
translations.34: And she conceived again, and bore a son; and she said: 'This time my husband shall turn to me — for I have borne him three sons.' And she named him Levi.
translations.35: And she conceived again, and bore a son; and she said: 'This time I shall thank God.' Therefore she named him Judah. And she ceased from bearing.
